subject: DPA negotiation — roles, logs, embeddings & execution path
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara.li@finservco.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: doconnor@finservco.com
Date: 2026-07-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: FinServCo DPA redline + questions on embeddings/telemetry

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — the product looks promising. Attached is our standard DPA with redlines (FinServCo-DPA-redline.docx). Before we get to signatures we have a few specific questions we want clarified in writing so our Privacy team can sign off:

- Role definitions: we currently have Redwood listed as Processor and FinServCo as Controller. We noticed language in section 2 that leaves room around derived assets (embeddings). Will Redwood accept Processor role for embeddings created from FinServCo data, or is there any claim to Controller status?

- Logs/telemetry: can you confirm what runtime logs you retain (request/response for debugging, sampling, metrics) vs what is retained for product telemetry/quality? What are default retention periods?

- Subprocessors and transfers: we need a subprocessors list and confirmation of EU->US transfer mechanisms (SCCs or other).

We'd like to get this wrapped up by the end of next week. Can you review and suggest redlines, and if possible share a DocuSign path so legal can route.

Best,
Sara Li
Head of Integrations, FinServCo

Attachments: FinServCo-DPA-redline.docx (docx, 48KB)

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@finservco.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, nikhil_sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinServCo DPA redline + questions on embeddings/telemetry

Hi Sara — thanks for sending this over and for the clear list of concerns. Looping in Marissa (sales lead) and Neha (privacy counsel) so we can provide precise language. Quick responses up front:

- Roles: Our standard position is that Redwood will act as Processor for customer data and any derived artifacts (including embeddings) generated from that customer data when created on behalf of the customer. We do not claim Controller status over customer raw data; for derived artifacts we recognize the need to be explicit and are prepared to accept Processor status in the DPA with carve-outs for aggregated, de-identified telemetry used for service improvement.

- Logs/telemetry: Operational logs (request IDs, timestamps, error traces) are retained short-term for debugging; default retention is 14 days, with an option for customers to request extended retention for troubleshooting under contract. Product telemetry and aggregated usage metrics used for model quality improvements are retained in an aggregated, non-identifiable form; we propose 90 days for telemetry aggregates.

- Subprocessors/transfers: we'll provide the subprocessors list and confirm SCCs for EU transfers.

Neha and Marissa — I attached a Redwood redline (Redwood_DPA_v3_redline.pdf) with specific clause language around embeddings, telemetry, and transfer mechanisms. I'll coordinate signatures once we converge on wording.

Thanks,
Laura
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3_redline.pdf (pdf, 72KB)

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@finservco.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinServCo DPA redline + questions on embeddings/telemetry

Sara — following up with a short summary of the key redlines we propose (full PDF attached). For quick review:

1) Definitions: add explicit definitions for "Derived Embeddings" and "Operational Logs".
   - Derived Embeddings: numerical vectors produced by applying models to Customer Data on behalf of the Customer; treated as Customer Data for the purposes of processing obligations, unless de-identified under section X.
   - Operational Logs: transient runtime diagnostics (request_id, error_code, latency, sampling indicators) used for debugging and metrics; not used for model training or feature engineering in identifiable form.

2) Controller/Processor: Redwood accepts Processor status for Customer Data and Derived Embeddings. We allow limited use of aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service improvement; this is explicitly prohibited for model training on identifiable customer data.

3) Retention: Operational Logs default 14 days, can be shortened to 0 or extended to up to 180 days by contractual agreement; telemetry aggregates 90 days.

4) Subprocessors & Transfers: we will provide an up-to-date subprocessors list and accept SCCs as the lawful transfer mechanism for EU->US. We'll include a DocuSign execution path once language is agreed.

If this summary looks good to you, we can incorporate any FinServCo redlines and then circulate the DocuSign envelope.

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: D. O'Connor <doconnor@finservco.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@finservco.com>
Date: 2026-07-22T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinServCo DPA redline + questions on embeddings/telemetry

Laura / Marissa — thanks for the quick turn. A few substantive points from our privacy team after reviewing your PDF and our redlines: 

- Embeddings: FinServCo's position is that embeddings derived from FinServCo personal data can remain "Customer Data" but in certain regulated contexts (financial profiling) we treat derivative vectors as pseudonymized outputs that the vendor must not repurpose. We are open to Processor treatment but we want a clause that explicitly prevents Redwood from using embeddings for any product training or third-party resale, period, without explicit, separate opt-in.

- Controller vs joint-controller: we cannot accept language that could be read to give Redwood unilateral discretionary use of aggregated telemetry as a separate legal basis for processing FinServCo personal data. If telemetry is used for model improvement we need either explicit anonymization standards or a joint-controller framework with narrow purposes.

- Logs: 14 days is acceptable in most cases, but for some backfills and audits we will ask for the option to request an extended window (we proposed 60 days).

Please propose exact warranty/repurpose prohibition language and the anonymization standard you reference. Also share the subprocessors list and the SCC template you'll rely on. We'll aim to circulate a final redline by Friday.

Regards,
Daniel O'Connor
Deputy GC, FinServCo

To: D. O'Connor <doconnor@finservco.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@finservco.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-22T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinServCo DPA redline + questions on embeddings/telemetry

Daniel / Sara — Neha from Redwood legal here. Thanks for the constructive feedback. Below are concrete clause proposals and commitments we can accept in the DPA redline to address each of your points. I've pasted the suggested language inline so it can be dropped into your docx: 

1) Embeddings/prohibition on repurpose: "Provider represents and warrants that it will not use Customer Data or Derived Embeddings for the purpose of training Provider's foundation models or for resale to third parties, except where Provider has obtained Customer's prior, express, and documented consent. Derived Embeddings shall be treated as Customer Data for the purposes of access, deletion, and export requests."

2) Telemetry/anonymization: "Provider may use aggregated telemetry and usage metrics for the sole purpose of monitoring and improving service quality. Aggregation must remove direct identifiers and be subject to a differential privacy noise floor or equivalent anonymization standard agreed in writing. Aggregated telemetry shall not be used to reconstruct Customer Data or to train models on identifiable customer content."

3) Controller/joint-controller: "Except as expressly set forth in this DPA, Provider is a Processor acting on Customer's documented instructions. Any narrow joint-controller arrangement for specific telemetry use-cases must be separately negotiated and documented with explicit purpose limitations."

4) Logs/retention: "Operational logs retained for debugging will default to 14 days. Customer may request an extended retention window for investigative purposes; Provider will accommodate requests up to 180 days subject to a negotiated fee and appropriate safeguards."

5) Transfers & Subprocessors: "Provider will supply an up-to-date subprocessors list and will execute SCCs for EU->US transfers. Provider shall notify Customer of material changes to subprocessors at least 30 days prior to onboarding."

If this language looks acceptable, we'll update the PDF/docx and share a DocuSign envelope. We can also include a DocuSign note that the DocuSign envelope ID will act as execution confirmation once signed by both parties.

—Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: D. O'Connor <doconnor@finservco.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@finservco.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, nikhil_sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-23T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Final — DPA agreed, DocuSign executed (envelope ID + next steps)

Daniel / Sara — great to have this across the finish line. Per Neha's proposed language we confirmed the following:

- Redwood = Processor for Customer Data and Derived Embeddings; explicit warranty against repurposing for model training or resale without consent.
- Aggregated telemetry permitted for service improvement only; must meet anonymization standard and cannot be used to train on identifiable customer content.
- Operational logs default retention 14 days; FinServCo may request up to 180 days for investigation with a fee.
- Redwood will provide subprocessors list and execute SCCs for cross-border transfers.

We updated the DPA with the agreed clauses and executed via DocuSign. DocuSign envelope ID: EXAMPLE-ENVELOPE-ID-12345. Final files attached.

Next steps:
- Laura/Marissa will post the signed DPA into the HubSpot deal record (FS-2026-041).
- Redwood will share the subprocessors list and SCC template link within 48 hours.
- FinServCo legal to confirm receipt and we can schedule kickoff for production onboarding.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Laura
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
